data.narrative:
CORE POWER is a Growth-stage climate and energy company that has raised $100M+. The valuation universe includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers across the sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient depth at CORE POWER's specific stage and valuation tier to support a robust peer-median approach.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary valuation signal. Using total raised ($100M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.2x multiplier typical of Growth-stage step-ups yields $120M. This method is applicable given CORE POWER's stage positioning but reflects a narrow methodological base. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable: while nine same-sector comparables exist, none of the tighter filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier—returned the minimum three datapoints needed for statistical reliability. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M (conservative case) to $138M (optimistic case), with a median point of $120M. This range reflects primarily the stage-progression method and carries material uncertainty given the single-method basis and sparse peer comparability at this frontier-tech, Growth-stage intersection. Key variables driving valuation remain capital efficiency, market adoption trajectory, and competitive positioning within the fragmented climate-tech landscape.
